clue.text: Plans drawn up for Napoleon's possible fate?

definitions.note: Napoleon is the ruling pig in Orwell's Animal Farm, and a pig may end up as tinned pork

indicators.note: in a down clue, drawn up means the word is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: plans are maps, as of a city or building

explanation.surface: Someone sketches out what might become of the French emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawn up' turns MAPS into SPAM. Napoleon here is not the emperor but the pig leader of Animal Farm; tinned pork is one fate for a pig.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinned spiced pork is a plausible end for a pig, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Smart answer picked up, then sleepy characters start to yawn

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: ZZ is the cartoon sign of someone snoozing

indicators.note: start to means only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A clever reply is heard, then a drowsy person begins to yawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' reverses ANS (answer) to SNA, then ZZ and the Y from 'start to yawn'.
explanation.definitionFit: Snazzy is an informal word for stylishly smart in dress or appearance.

clue.text: Unbalanced measure of bitter plant

parts.note: cuckoo is slang for crazy or mentally unbalanced
bitter is a British beer, served by the pint

explanation.surface: A deranged pub order of a glass of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a type of British beer, usually ordered by the pint; 'bitter plant' looks like one phrase but splits after bitter.
explanation.definitionFit: The cuckoo-pint is the wild arum, a common British woodland plant also called lords-and-ladies.

clue.text: Decent time in pursuit

indicators.note: in places the time letter inside the word for pursuit

parts.note: a pursuit is a chase

explanation.surface: A respectable interval spent in pursuit of someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts T (time) inside CHASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means pure and modest, morally decent in conduct.

clue.text: 'ang out among lovers of good ale, lifting drink

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting means the whole assembly is read upwards
among puts the dropped-aitch word inside the group of beer lovers

parts.note: CAMRA, the Campaign for Real Ale, is the British group devoted to traditional beer
hang with its H dropped, as the apostrophe shows, leaves ANG

explanation.surface: Hanging about with real-ale fans and raising a glass.
explanation.walkthrough: CAMRA is Britain's Campaign for Real Ale. 'among' sets the dropped-aitch word just after its first letter, giving CANGAMRA, and 'lifting' reads that upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Armagnac is a brandy from Gascony in south-west France, so a drink.

clue.text: As such, the sum of all parts limited

definitions.text: As such, the sum of all parts limited

parts.words: As such, the sum of all parts limited
parts.note: read as an actor whose whole range of roles is restricted to one kind of character

explanation.surface: In that case, the total of every component is capped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' are acting roles: an actor given only one kind of role has a career whose sum of parts is limited.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor confined to one kind of role finds the whole range of roles offered narrow.

clue.text: Fit as a fiddle? I suppose so

definitions.meaning: a grudging phrase of agreement, like all right then

explanation.surface: Asked if they are in good health, someone answers with a reluctant yes.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both in fine health and a reluctant all right, I agree.

clue.text: Cutter counts out loud

indicators.note: out loud means the word for counts is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: to count up is to add, so counts means adds

explanation.surface: A tally is announced aloud by someone with a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out loud' signals that ADDS (counts) sounds like the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: An adze is an axe-like tool with an arched blade for cutting and shaping wood.

clue.text: Confine drug dealer whose work is mind-numbing

definitions.note: stands for a person with tedious work

parts.note: to pen is to shut in or confine
a pusher is someone who sells illegal drugs

explanation.surface: Lock up the dealer whose job is so tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description of a person: one whose work is mind-numbing.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen-pusher is a clerk doing dull routine office paperwork, a job thought tedious.

clue.text: Give all you've got as a farmer

definitions.text: all you've got as a farmer
definitions.meaning: the total crop a farmer harvests

explanation.surface: Hand over everything a farmer produces.
explanation.definitionFit: Yield means both to give way and the total produce harvested from land.

clue.text: Noted irritation in public places

parts.note: read noted as made of musical notes: an annoying music played in shops and lifts

explanation.surface: An annoyance that people remark on when out and about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' seems to mean remarked upon, but it means consisting of musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Bland recorded background music piped into shops and lifts irritates many people.

clue.text: Extra weight carried by plea from bombarded citizens of Lebanon?

definitions.meaning: a roll of fat round the waist

definitions.text: plea from bombarded citizens of Lebanon?
definitions.meaning: Tyre is a city in Lebanon, so its people might beg the attackers to leave it unharmed

explanation.surface: Excess weight is carried by a Lebanese call for mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyre is an ancient port city in southern Lebanon; read as 'spare Tyre!' it is a plea for mercy.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare tyre is a slang term for a roll of fat around the middle, and literally a plea to save Tyre.

clue.text: Might European dance round it once a year?

definitions.text: dance round it once a year?
definitions.note: describes a thing that people dance around on an annual festival

parts.note: may and might both express possibility
a Pole is a person from Poland, a European

explanation.surface: Could someone from Europe join an annual dance?
explanation.walkthrough: 'dance round it' describes the thing danced round: a tall decorated pole at May Day festivities.
explanation.definitionFit: Dancers circle a ribboned pole each May Day in traditional English celebrations.

clue.text: Demonstration that may be stolen

definitions.meaning: the idiom is to steal a lead on rivals by acting first

explanation.surface: A protest that someone might pinch.
explanation.walkthrough: To steal a march on someone is to gain an advantage by acting first.
explanation.definitionFit: A march is a protest walk, and one steals a march when gaining an early advantage.

clue.text: London university admitted to threatening sort of war

indicators.note: admitted to means let inside the next word

parts.note: something threatening is near or imminent
UCL is University College London

explanation.surface: A college in the capital was drawn into a menacing conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted to' signals the container; 'threatening' here means imminent, as a storm is near, not menacing.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear war is a kind of war fought with atomic weapons.

clue.text: What prosecutor seeks with assurance

explanation.surface: A lawyer pursues a verdict confidently.
explanation.definitionFit: A conviction is both a guilty verdict and a firmly held, certain belief.

clue.text: Hot, like South African capital?

parts.note: capital as money: the rand is South Africa's currency
the suffix -y forms adjectives meaning like or having the quality of

explanation.surface: Sultry weather, as in Pretoria?
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like a city such as Pretoria but means money: the rand.
explanation.definitionFit: Randy is informal for lustful, sexually aroused, just as hot can mean.

clue.text: Religious teacher docking tail of animal

indicators.note: docking cuts off the tail, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a rabbit is an animal

explanation.surface: A clergyman cuts off the tail of a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docking tail of' removes the final T of RABBIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish scholar and teacher of religious law.

clue.text: Sight of adolescent boy's face, unfortunate mistake!

parts.note: bum is slang for bad or unlucky, as in a bum deal
a fluff is a bungled attempt or blunder

explanation.surface: A teenager's face is a bad error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bum' as an adjective (a bum deal) means poor or unlucky; a fluff is a botched shot or line.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumfluff is British slang for the thin first beard growth on a teenage boy's face.

clue.text: Jock (not PC!)

definitions.meaning: a computer made by Apple rather than a Windows PC

explanation.surface: A Scotsman refuses political correctness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PC' looks like political correctness but is personal computer; Mac is also a form of address for a Scotsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Mac is slang for a Scot and also an Apple computer, the rival of the PC.

clue.text: Girl snatches boy up, which is saucy

definitions.note: describes something made as a sauce

indicators.note: snatches means the girl's name grabs and holds the other piece

parts.note: Marie is a girl's name

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: Dan is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A girl grabs a lad, which is rather cheeky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the boy to NAD and 'snatches' signals the container. 'saucy' looks like cheeky but means sauce-like.
explanation.definitionFit: A marinade is a seasoned liquid sauce in which food is soaked.

clue.text: Material only woven before noon

indicators.note: before puts the rearranged letters ahead of the next piece
woven suggests strands interlaced, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Only cloth is woven before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woven' rearranges the word only, which is then set 'before' the noon letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic fibre used as a fabric, a material.

clue.text: First of mice and rats he experimented with, creating relative

indicators.note: experimented with means these letters are tried in new arrangements
first of takes just the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A scientist tested mice and rats and produced a related creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'experimented with' rearranges M (the first of mice) with RATS and HE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamster is a rodent, so a relative of mice and rats.

clue.text: Easy entering via Tommy's home

indicators.note: entering puts the word for easy inside the word for via

parts.note: via means by way of, so by
light means easy, as in light work

explanation.surface: A simple route home for a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' signals the container. Tommy (Tommy Atkins) is the nickname for a British private soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Blighty is old soldiers' slang for Britain, home to the British Tommy.

clue.text: Runs into savage, which so soothed by music?

definitions.note: refers to the saying that music soothes the savage part of a person

indicators.note: into puts the runs letter inside the word for savage

parts.note: a savage is a brute or beast
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A rush into a wild creature, calmed by a tune?
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts R (runs) inside BEAST. The definition alludes to Congreve's line 'Music has charms to soothe a savage breast'.
explanation.definitionFit: Congreve wrote that music has charms to soothe a savage breast, the one thing so calmed.

clue.text: What man joining police has left on top?

definitions.text: What man joining police has left on top?

indicators.note: on top places the left letter above the police in a down clue

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

explanation.surface: What does a new police recruit keep on his head?
explanation.walkthrough: 'on top' sets the left letter above the police in this down entry; the whole clue also describes a policeman's headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: A policeman's tall headgear is a helmet, worn on top of the head.

clue.text: Shows permit?

parts.note: read as a permit for watching shows, the British fee for owning a television

explanation.surface: Does the evidence allow it?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shows' reads as a verb but is a plural noun: television programmes. Britain requires a paid licence to watch TV.
explanation.definitionFit: A British permit to watch broadcast programmes is needed by law.

clue.text: Go for a spin

definitions.meaning: a go or chance in a game, as in your go
a short drive or trip, or a rotation

explanation.surface: Head off for a drive.
explanation.definitionFit: A turn is both someone's go in a game and a short spin or rotation.

clue.text: See 6
Accent has come about in Latinised literature

indicators.note: come about means turned round, so the letters read backwards
in means the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A diacritic has appeared in Romanised writing.
explanation.walkthrough: The run EDLIT sits 'in' Latinised literature, and 'come about' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A tilde is the wavy accent mark placed over a letter, as in Spanish n.

clue.text: Powerless, insignificant artist

indicators.note: less the power letter: P, the symbol for power, is removed

parts.note: petty means trivial or insignificant

explanation.surface: A weak, minor painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Powerless' removes P (power) from PETTY. William Etty was an English painter known for nudes.
explanation.definitionFit: William Etty was a nineteenth-century English painter, so an artist.

clue.text: Controversial habit backing Guardian crossword setter

indicators.note: backing means the word is turned to read backwards

parts.note: wearing fur is a contentious fashion habit
the Guardian refers to itself as us

explanation.surface: A disputed practice is supported by the newspaper's puzzle compiler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns FUR into RUF; US is the Guardian speaking of itself. Rufus was a Guardian crossword setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rufus was the pseudonym of Roger Squires, a prolific Guardian crossword compiler.

clue.text: Serve old home, unlike faithful servant?

definitions.note: describes the opposite of a trustworthy worker

parts.note: to dish up food is to serve it
a nest is a home

explanation.surface: Dish up at the old house, unlike a loyal retainer.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'good and faithful servant': being the opposite of faithful means untrustworthy.
explanation.definitionFit: A faithful servant is trustworthy, so one unlike him is deceitful and untruthful.
